LESSON: MAGNETISM

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 4.2: Magnetism

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Magnetism. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya
3. practise Magnetism in clear steps
4. apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MAGNETISM
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Magnetism helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: MAGNETISM
Study Magnetism like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Magnetism” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Magnetism matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Magnetism in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Magnetism in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Magnetism in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Magnetism this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Magnetism in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Magnetism” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Magnetism is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Magnetism” around your school. (skill: explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Magnetism matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Magnetism this week. (skill: practise Magnetism in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Magnetism” around your school. (skill: apply Magnetism in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Magnetism to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Magnetism in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Magnetism from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Magnetism: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Magnetism?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Magnetism means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Magnetism means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Magnetism from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
